headline: Tariff threat sharpens deal push as Nifty eyes its best month in six years

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the twenty-seventh of November, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, Washington's proposed tariff of up to 25 percent on Indian goods is still the talk of the town. Exporters want a deal signed quickly, because a deal would bring that rate down to 17 percent.

Second, the market is on a strong run. The Nifty is up more than 12 percent in November, on course for its best month since April 2020. Foreign investors have now bought Indian shares for twelve sessions in a row.

And third, Mahanadi Coalfields, the Coal India unit, makes its stock market debut today. It's the first listing since the market regulator barred the publishing of grey market prices for IPO shares.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
The Nifty ended Thursday at 25,884 and a half, with both the Sensex and the Nifty near ten-month highs. The index spent much of the day just below the flat line, while realty stole the show. The Nifty Realty index rose about 3 percent to a fifty-two-week high, led by Prestige Estates and Brigade Enterprises. Brigade said it sold homes worth 1,600 crore rupees in the launch weekend of a Bengaluru project.

Among the big names, HDFC Bank has climbed about 30 percent from its October low and overtook Bharti Airtel to become the second most valuable listed company, at around 13.4 lakh crore rupees. Wipro rose 4 percent on a new partnership with BP. And the exchange stocks keep running. NSE shares are up 9 percent in two days, taking its value close to 6 lakh crore rupees. Livemint reports that makes it the world's third largest listed exchange, ahead of Nasdaq and the London Stock Exchange.

Now to the flows. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth about 5,843 crore rupees on Thursday, and domestic institutional investors added about 5,631 crore rupees.

The levels to watch: analysts see 26,000 as the immediate hurdle on the Nifty, then 26,200. Support sits at 25,800, and then the 25,600 to 25,700 zone. For the Bank Nifty, they want it to hold 63,000 and cross 64,000. Early signals from GIFT Nifty are mixed this morning, with most pointing to a muted start, as the market eyes a fifth straight weekly gain.

On the outlook, J P Morgan calls Indian shares a safe haven from the global A I trade and sees the Nifty at 29,000 by the end of 2027. PL Capital has raised its twelve-month Nifty target to about 28,560.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
On the IPO front, Mahanadi Coalfields lists today after an offer worth about 969 million dollars. Crystal Crop Protection listed on Thursday at a premium of about 2 to 3 percent, after its issue was subscribed seventeen times. Coming up, diaper maker Swara Baby Products opens an 800 crore rupee IPO on the second of December, with a price band of 105 to 111 rupees. Its shares are due to list on the ninth. Meanwhile, Pentacle Consultants and Bvishal Oil and Energy have withdrawn their draft papers. And the regulator is moving to cut off the commercial incentives for regulated firms that promote grey market premiums, which it likens to betting.

Now to the deals. The South Korean parent of LG Electronics India sold a 2 percent stake, taking its holding from 85 to 83 percent, and the shares fell over 3 percent. The promoter of Schaeffler India sold 6 and a half percent, yet the stock rose nearly 3 percent. Capital Group sold over 1 percent of IIFL Finance.

The IDBI Bank sale has entered a crucial stage. The disinvestment secretary says the Reserve Bank is examining Fairfax as a bidder. The Cabinet has also approved Prudential's foreign investment in Bharti Life Insurance.

One more boardroom battle to note. Tata Trusts has decided to go to the Bombay High Court to challenge the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman of Tata Sons, and Tata stocks traded mixed on the news. And Supriya Lifescience will consider a share buyback on the second of December, after its September quarter profit fell 42 percent to about 29 crore rupees.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, and the rupee came under pressure on Thursday. It settled at 92.44 to the dollar as crude climbed, and the ten-year government bond yield rose 7 basis points to 7.24 percent.

On tariffs, the reaction to Washington's proposal is split. Exporters' body president S C Ralhan wants a deal as soon as possible, saying orders from American buyers are strong. But his colleague Ajay Sahai warns that even 17 percent may give little edge, as South East Asian rivals could get better terms. He estimates an extra cost of about 8 percent for exporters if the rate goes to 25. Moneycontrol's analysis finds India could win close to 3 billion dollars of Vietnam's exports to America, while garments and electrical equipment are most exposed. ASSOCHAM still expects total exports to cross 1 trillion dollars this financial year.

From the Reserve Bank, its first switch auction for state bonds drew 8,003 crore rupees, with Tamil Nadu the largest share, and traders now expect more such rounds. The Reserve Bank has also cleared the National Stock Exchange to launch corporate bond index futures. Its bulletin shows non-bank lenders now rely on banks for nearly 40 percent of their borrowing, and gold loans grew 75 percent last financial year to 3.67 lakh crore rupees.

On the Budget, the government is reported to see crude settling at 80 to 85 dollars a barrel, and may use that for next year's numbers. The Finance Minister also held her first pre-Budget meeting with young people.

Two Supreme Court matters for you. The court has asked HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to sanction the prosecution of staff in the builder subvention scheme cases, within a week. And it has suggested Parliament amend section 26E of the SARFAESI Act, to define what all other debts means for secured creditors' priority.

And one sobering number: infrastructure projects carry a cost overrun of 3.28 lakh crore rupees, as of October.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil is back in focus. Brent crude has crossed 96 dollars a barrel, trading near 97, after a Houthi attack on a key Saudi refinery. It's up about 4 and a half percent this week, set for its first weekly gain this month.

American markets were shut for Thanksgiving, but stronger than expected core inflation data has firmed up the case for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. That has pushed the dollar close to a twenty-two-month high, and kept gold near a fifteen-month low, around 3,560 dollars an ounce.

In Asia, shares rose for a second day as nerves over the A I trade eased. Japan's Nikkei gained 0.7 percent and South Korea's Kospi 1.5 percent. Still, the Bank of England has warned that the big A I firms' financial exposure has passed 4 trillion dollars, which it says raises risks across markets. And Bitcoin is back above 60,000 dollars, though it is still down by more than half from its peak.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India and US trade deal you're following. A day after Washington put a price on the deal, 17 percent with an agreement and up to 25 without, exporters urged the government to sign quickly. The brokerage Jefferies said the threat is likely to hasten the deal, while a traders' body called for a 25 percent retaliatory duty if the higher rate goes ahead.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. December is a busy month on the tax calendar, with T D S payments, the next advance tax instalment, the last window for belated returns, and the FAST-DS scheme all due. And if you hold foreign shares through stock options or restricted stock units, Livemint has a useful guide on correcting past gaps in foreign asset disclosure, including the related brokerage accounts.

If you have an old provident fund account with no deposits for three years, check it. The provident fund body says such accounts can turn inoperative and stop earning interest. You can claim the balance with Form 19, or move it to your new employer with Form 13, once your K Y C is updated.

For government staff, dearness allowance has gone up by 3 points to 63 percent, and the Eighth Pay Commission is expected to report by May 2027. On deposits, Punjab National Bank's special 680-day deposit offers up to about seven and a half percent. Federal Bank now lets eligible customers open a pension account instantly under the Tatkal N P S scheme. And with gold falling, only two gold exchange traded funds show positive returns over the past year.

One investor warning. The market regulator has barred Le Lavoir, its chairman and thirteen others over alleged price manipulation and diversion of issue money, acting before a share lock-in was due to expire.

That's the brief. Today, watch the Mahanadi Coalfields debut, whether the Nifty can finally clear 26,000 and close out a fifth weekly gain, and how crude near 97 dollars weighs on the rupee. Have a good Friday.
